title: LOD & LOI — Level of Development and Level of Information

scope.purpose: Define paired geometric and non-graphical information expectations, model progression, milestone readiness, and permitted reliance across the lifecycle of governed model information.
scope.boundary: This standard governs progression and authorized-use principles. Project-specific stage names, discipline mappings, detailed element expectations, and milestone criteria belong in governed project requirements and BEP instruments unless separately curated as reusable standards.

requirements.statement: Visual completeness shall not imply coordination, fabrication readiness, engineering approval, contractual authority, or permission for downstream use.
Level of Information requirements shall be paired with Level of Development definitions for every modeled element category.
LOD 400 fabrication elements shall be validated against vendor shop drawings prior to construction issuance.
Model progression shall be governed by declared purpose, authorized use, geometric and non-geometric information expectations, and responsible scope rather than by visual appearance alone.
Model information shall not be relied upon beyond its declared progression state, permitted use, or stated information maturity without an explicitly governed change in authorization.
Each governed information milestone shall define the criteria by which the applicable model scope or deliverable package is assessed for its declared purpose and downstream use.
Progression criteria shall identify the information author or responsible scope and the receiving or relying party where those distinctions affect readiness, permitted use, or handoff.

Project BEPs and information requirements may refine progression stages and discipline-specific criteria, but such refinements shall preserve explicit purpose, permitted-use boundaries, and traceability to governed information requirements.

Progression and maturity may vary by element, system, discipline, or scope; readiness shall therefore be assessed against the declared requirements for the relevant scope rather than assumed to be uniform across an entire model.

source_stage_examples.note: The supporting source presents these stages schematically and permits project BEPs to refine them. They are retained as source evidence only and are not promoted here as a mandatory enterprise stage vocabulary.

showset_permitted_use.LOD100: Narrative alignment and early spatial exploration; not for fabrication or clearance sign-off.
showset_permitted_use.LOD200: Thematic coordination and initial interfaces; not for final clearances or pricing commitments.
showset_permitted_use.LOD300: Clash detection, coordinated drawings basis, and design intent documentation; not fabrication-ready.
showset_permitted_use.LOD350: Detailed clash resolution and interface/penetration coordination; not final shop model.
showset_permitted_use.LOD400: Fabrication planning and shop/CNC derivation subject to QA/QC.
showset_permitted_use.LOD500: Field-verified operations reference and retrofit planning.

provenance.migration_note: Core L4 LOD/LOI source enriched from the model-progression source. Durable progression, authorized-use, milestone, responsibility, and non-uniform-maturity principles were normalized into requirements. Source stage names remain informative because the supporting progression page is draft and explicitly allows project refinement.
